nodes.label: Recommerce-Owned Tracked-Receiving Service
nodes.rationale: A narrow Recommerce-owned receiving service and screen calls existing Ultimate POS purchase/quantity utilities inside one database transaction, then creates the Device and receipt-assignment evidence before commit. This limits the initial write surface to one reviewed workflow and permits explicit unit ordering, one idempotency key, one transaction boundary and a deterministic unit-to-purchase-line link.

nodes.label: Proposed Receiving Transaction Sequence
nodes.rationale: Eleven ordered steps from authorization through idempotency validation, core row locking, core purchase creation, per-unit Device creation, evidence recording and commit. Any failure before commit rolls back both core purchase effects and Recommerce rows; a failure after commit must recover the original outcome rather than repeat the purchase.

nodes.label: Tracked-Receiving Invariants
nodes.rationale: One physical unit has one Device; a Device links to one approved core receipt line; core aggregate quantity stays authoritative; retry does not duplicate; neither side can survive the other's failure; printing does not create identity; scan-only view does not mutate stock; Repair is untouched.

nodes.label: Receiving Idempotency Key and Stored Outcome
nodes.rationale: A unique operation/idempotency receipt with a stored outcome makes browser and scanner retry safe: a duplicate key returns the original outcome and a conflicting reused key is rejected without mutation.

nodes.label: Rejected Alternative: Post-Commit Purchase Event Only
nodes.rationale: Rejected as the sole contract because the event identifies a purchase transaction but does not necessarily carry one validated physical unit per quantity, risking ambiguous assignment, delayed failure and non-reconcilable stock.

nodes.label: Deferred Alternative: Generic Core Purchase Hook
nodes.rationale: Deferred because the checkout does not prove a stable purchase-form module hook, and a generic hook could change ordinary purchase behavior or expose an uncontrolled Recommerce write path.

nodes.label: Rejected Alternative: Separate Recommerce Stock Authority
nodes.rationale: Rejected because Ultimate POS remains authoritative for aggregate catalogue quantity, transactions, payments and accounting; Recommerce records physical-unit identity and evidence and reconciles to core quantity.

nodes.label: Deferred Alternative: Asynchronous Queue for First Receipt
nodes.rationale: Deferred because the installed configuration defaults to synchronous queues and an asynchronous split would make core purchase/Device atomicity harder to prove; Alpha uses a transaction-local synchronous service.

nodes.label: Required Proof Before Implementation Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Eleven named tests spanning success, validation failure, core posting failure, duplicate and conflicting idempotency keys, concurrent identical identifiers, post-commit label failure, unchanged behavior with Recommerce off, alternative stock paths and cross-business denial; most pass only against a local disposable SQLite proof.
